reference: Apology of al-Kindi, Christian reply, Arabic: the Aisha and Safwan b. al-Mu'attal episode (sentence beginning 'وكذلك هناته مع عائشة'); Muir 1882 pp. 9 (footnote 1, p. 60 lines 4 and 6 of the Arabic)
gist_en: The author narrates Aisha's journey back with Safwan and the slander, and then Muhammad's favouritism; Muir calls the passage objectionable.
why_excluded: Sexually charged scandal narrative (adultery accusation). Muir himself calls the passage objectionable. The sentence that closes this story (kindi-AGE-01) is quoted alone because it contains no details of the scandal.

reference: Apology of al-Kindi, Christian reply, Arabic: remarks on individual wives (Umm Salama, Zaynab bint Jahsh, Safiyya, Muleika, Rayhana etc.), Muir 1882 p. 10
gist_en: The author comments on the sexual conduct and marriage bargains of several wives and on the Prophet's marital affairs, including a crude anecdote about a wife and a sexual offer.
why_excluded: Sexually suggestive anecdotes; does not name Aisha in the same passage beyond the list; not needed for the Aisha finding. Kept out of passages.json.

reference: Apology of al-Kindi, OpenITI 0300Anonymous.RisalataHashimiWaKindi.SyriacStudies00001-ara1, same sentence as kindi-AGE-01 (variant 'وكانت خلابة')
gist_en: Second Arabic transcription of the same Aisha sentence; differs in adding 'and she was bewitching'.
why_excluded: Duplicate of kindi-AGE-01 with a textual variant; the Kalema text was used as the base. The variant is recorded in passages.json limits.

reference: Michael the Syrian, Chronique (Chabot, French, vol. 2, Book XI ch. 2, p. 407, Syriac original not read); archive.org MichelLeSyrien2
gist_en: Michael describes the Arabs' teaching: four free wives and as many concubines as they like, and a passion for worldly and carnal pleasures.
why_excluded: General polygamy description; no Aisha, no age. Not one of the five kinds. Negative result for the lead.

reference: Bar Hebraeus, Chronicon Syriacum (Bruns & Kirsch 1789, Latin, Dynasty X, pp. 102-103, Narratio de confessione Arabica)
gist_en: The Arabic 'confession' narrative says the Prophet's followers were allowed carnal desires, polygamy with free women and concubines, and repudiation; Khadija is named, Abu Bakr is called his father-in-law.
why_excluded: No Aisha in this narrative and no age; the polygamy criticism is general. Kept as a lead for the orchestrator; not a passage under the team's five kinds.

reference: Kiracos de Gantzac (Kirakos Gandzaketsi), trad. Brosset 1870, Deux historiens arméniens, approx. p. 30-31 (page inferred from OCR page marker; not verified)
gist_en: Kirakos says Mahmet promised a material paradise with 'continual intercourse with women who remain virgins' and attacks his laws.
why_excluded: Sexual content of a paradise description; no Aisha; no marriage criticism of the Prophet's wives. Not selected.

gist_en: Ibn Hazm's 'al-Risala al-Bahira' is on the duty to follow the Companions over jurists; Aisha appears only as one of several Companions.
why_excluded: Not about the monk Bahira legend (the title means 'the brilliant epistle'); Aisha appears only in a list of Companions. Negative result.
